title: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit
description_short: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit
description_medium: Representative Eric Swalwell sued Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Rudy Giuliani and Representative Mo Brooks over the January 6 attack, alleging they conspired to obstruct Congress’s electoral count and incite violence. On March 24, 2021, reports said campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall would represent the Trumps. The appointment was a development in a pending case, not a ruling on Swalwell’s claims.
description_long:
Representative Eric Swalwell filed a civil lawsuit on March 5, 2021, against Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Rudy Giuliani and Representative Mo Brooks. He alleged that they conspired to obstruct Congress’s certification of Joe Biden’s victory and incite the violence at the Capitol on January 6. The complaint also invoked District of Columbia laws concerning inciting a riot and terrorism.

On March 24, reports said Jesse Binnall would represent the Trumps. Binnall had worked on Trump’s campaign legal team and represented Trump in other election-related disputes. His role in the case was a procedural development; it did not resolve the allegations or establish the defendants’ liability. The lawsuit remained pending at the time of the report. The account does not include the defendants’ responses or a later court decision, so the claims should be described as allegations made by Swalwell. The event was the selection of counsel in litigation arising from January 6, alongside the civil claims against the former president and the other defendants.
organization_tags: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia

title: Trump: Hungarian and Russian officials caught on intercepts coordinating to block Ukraine from EU
description_short: Trump: Hungarian and Russian officials caught on intercepts coordinating to block Ukraine from EU
description_medium: An investigative report said an intercepted December 2023 call captured Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó briefing Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during EU talks on Ukraine’s membership. The report said Hungary’s Viktor Orbán threatened a veto and Lavrov praised the pressure strategy. EU leaders nevertheless opened accession negotiations with Ukraine; the reported call did not show Hungary succeeded in blocking them.
description_long:
During a December 14, 2023, European Council meeting in Brussels, EU leaders discussed opening membership negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova. An investigative report said Hungary’s Prime Minister Viktor Orbán threatened to veto the move while disputing the European Union’s withholding of more than €22 billion in funds over rule-of-law concerns.

The report described an intercepted call in which Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó left the meeting to speak with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. In the quoted exchange, Szijjártó explained Hungary’s approach to the meeting, and Lavrov praised the strategy as “direct blackmailing.” The reporters characterized the conversation as evidence of coordination between Hungarian and Russian officials around the veto threat. EU leaders ultimately opened accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova at that meeting, so the episode did not result in blocking Ukraine’s next step. The claim rests on the reported intercept and should be attributed to the investigation; it is not an official finding by the EU. The account documents the discussion, not the officials’ full motives or every detail of the interception.

title: Trump: Senior U.S. Treasury official quits after DOGE attempts to access sensitive payment systems
description_short: Trump: Senior U.S. Treasury official quits after DOGE attempts to access sensitive payment systems
description_medium: Treasury career official David A. Lebryk announced his retirement on January 31, 2025, after a dispute with Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency over access to payment systems. The Bureau of the Fiscal Service processes more than $6 trillion in annual federal payments, including Social Security, Medicare, salaries and tax refunds. Lebryk had served at Treasury since 1989.
description_long:
David A. Lebryk, Treasury’s highest-ranking career official, announced his retirement on January 31, 2025, after a dispute with representatives of Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency over access to federal payment systems. Lebryk had served at Treasury since 1989 and was acting secretary during the transition until Scott Bessent was confirmed.

The Bureau of the Fiscal Service operates the system, which processes more than $6 trillion in payments each year, including Social Security and Medicare benefits, federal salaries and tax refunds. Access had been limited to a small group of career officials because the system moves sensitive funds. Reporting said DOGE representatives sought access after the 2024 election and intensified their requests after Trump took office. Treasury staff considered the request unusual and raised concerns about the safeguards. Lebryk’s retirement followed the dispute, but the linked account did not quote him explaining his decision. The episode focused attention on which officials could access federal payment infrastructure and how those systems were protected during the transition.

title: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers
description_short: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers
description_medium: A French space researcher was reportedly searched at Houston’s airport after officials found messages criticizing the Trump administration’s science policy on the researcher’s phone. The researcher’s devices were reportedly confiscated and the person was returned to Europe the next day. French minister Philippe Baptiste said the messages expressed a personal opinion; the researcher’s name and the legal basis for refusing entry were not reported.
description_long:
The linked account reported that a French space researcher was stopped at a Houston airport in March 2025. U.S. officials allegedly searched the researcher’s work computer and personal phone and found messages criticizing the Trump administration’s treatment of scientists. The researcher was reportedly sent back to Europe the following day, without the devices. The account did not identify the person or explain the legal basis for refusing entry.

Philippe Baptiste, France’s minister for higher education and research, said the messages were exchanges with colleagues and friends expressing a personal view of U.S. research policy. He criticized the decision by U.S. authorities. The reports also said the researcher had published an open letter inviting American scientists to move to France. The account documents a reported device search and denial of entry linked to private messages, while leaving the researcher’s identity, the agency’s explanation and the legal grounds unclear. Baptiste’s public response made the incident a diplomatic concern as well as a question about border searches and travelers’ expression.
organization_tags: French Ministry of Higher Education and Research

title: Trump allies draft executive order to take control over elections
description_short: Trump allies draft executive order to take control over elections
description_medium: Trump allies circulated a draft executive order proposing federal control over election procedures, including bans on mail ballots and voting machines. The draft invoked foreign interference as a national-security justification but was not signed by Trump. Lawyer Peter Ticktin and activist Cleta Mitchell promoted it; Ticktin acknowledged that states ordinarily administer elections and argued that an alleged foreign threat could justify federal action.
description_long:
On April 12, 2025, Trump allies circulated a draft executive order proposing federal control over election procedures, including bans on mail-in voting and voting machines. The draft invoked foreign interference as a national-security rationale. Its circulation did not make it an executive order: Trump did not sign it, and states retain a central role in administering elections.

Florida lawyer Peter Ticktin promoted the proposal. He said a president normally lacked authority over how states conduct elections, but argued that an alleged foreign threat could justify federal action. Election activist and lawyer Cleta Mitchell was also involved. The linked account said the activists claimed to be coordinating with the White House, but it did not establish that the administration adopted the draft. The document records an effort by Trump allies to expand presidential authority over voting, not a policy that took effect. The difference between a circulated proposal and a signed directive determines its legal status and practical effect.

preserved_fields.title: Trump allies draft executive order to take control over elections
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump allies draft executive order to take control over elections

title: Trump orders DOJ investigation of ActBlue, largest Democrat fundraising platform
description_short: Trump orders DOJ investigation of ActBlue, largest Democrat fundraising platform
description_medium: Trump signed a memorandum directing Attorney General Pam Bondi to investigate allegations of straw and foreign donations through online fundraising platforms, amid scrutiny of ActBlue. It cited a House report that ActBlue had detected 22 significant fraud campaigns and 237 donations from foreign IP addresses using prepaid cards. Those figures did not establish that ActBlue committed fraud; the memorandum ordered an investigation.
description_long:
On April 24, 2025, Trump signed a memorandum directing Attorney General Pam Bondi, in consultation with the Treasury secretary, to investigate allegations that online fundraising platforms were used for straw or foreign political contributions. The memorandum followed Republican scrutiny of ActBlue, a major fundraising platform used by Democratic candidates and organizations.

The directive cited a House investigation that said ActBlue had detected at least 22 significant fraud campaigns, nearly half with a foreign connection, and 237 donations from foreign IP addresses using prepaid cards during a 30-day period in the 2024 campaign. Those figures described activity the platform said it had detected; they were not findings that ActBlue knowingly accepted illegal donations. Trump’s memorandum ordered an investigation and enforcement if warranted. It did not announce charges or establish that the allegations were true. The document did not mention WinRed, the major Republican fundraising platform, a difference that raised questions about the scope of the administration’s scrutiny.

preserved_fields.title: Trump orders DOJ investigation of ActBlue, largest Democrat fundraising platform
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump orders DOJ investigation of ActBlue, largest Democrat fundraising platform

title: Trump: DHS official says more arrests of Democratic lawmakers are coming
description_short: Trump: DHS official says more arrests of Democratic lawmakers are coming
description_medium: After ICE detained Newark Mayor Ras Baraka outside an immigration facility, DHS spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin said more arrests of Democratic lawmakers were “likely.” She said the department had body-camera footage of lawmakers assaulting officers and that arrests were under consideration. The statement was not an announcement of charges or completed arrests, and the supplied report does not identify the lawmakers or show the footage.
description_long:
On May 10, 2025, Department of Homeland Security spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin told CNN that more arrests were possible after ICE detained Newark Mayor Ras Baraka during a visit to an immigration facility. She said DHS had body-camera footage showing members of Congress assaulting officers and that arresting lawmakers who were present was “definitely on the table” as part of an investigation.

McLaughlin also said Baraka had “stormed” the facility. The linked account said footage showed him being taken into custody outside the gate; Baraka opposed the facility in Newark. Her comments described possible future enforcement, not additional arrests or charges that had already occurred. The episode linked a local dispute over an ICE facility to a federal investigation involving the mayor and visiting lawmakers. The public account did not identify the lawmakers or include the body-camera footage, and it did not report later charging decisions. McLaughlin’s statement was a warning about contemplated action, rather than confirmation of a completed case.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: DHS official says more arrests of Democratic lawmakers are coming
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: DHS official says more arrests of Democratic lawmakers are coming

title: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks
description_short: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks
description_medium: The Guardian reported that White House advisers lost confidence in a Pentagon leak investigation after Pete Hegseth’s lawyer, Tim Parlatore, said a warrantless wiretap found classified material on an aide’s phone. Parlatore later denied saying a wiretap was used and said he was repeating information from Pentagon officials. The investigation was reassigned; the reporting did not establish that either man knowingly lied.
description_long:
The Guardian reported a breakdown in trust between the White House and Pentagon during an investigation into leaks of military information. Tim Parlatore, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s personal lawyer and the person overseeing the inquiry, told White House advisers that investigators had used a warrantless wiretap to find classified material on the phone of Dan Caldwell, then a senior Hegseth adviser.

When White House officials questioned how Parlatore knew about the alleged wiretap, he later denied that one had taken place and said Pentagon officials had supplied the information. The report said the Air Force Office of Special Investigations had initially focused on mid-level aides and later turned to Caldwell and two others around the time they were fired. Caldwell maintained his innocence. The leak investigation was transferred from Parlatore to Deputy Defense Secretary Stephen Feinberg. The reporting describes conflicting accounts about how the wiretap claim arose and a loss of confidence in the inquiry; it does not establish that Hegseth or Parlatore knowingly made a false statement.
organization_tags: Air Force Office of Special Investigations

title: Trump pulls nomination of NASA head for no clear reason
description_short: Trump pulls nomination of NASA head for no clear reason
description_medium: On May 31, 2025, Trump withdrew Jared Isaacman’s nomination to lead NASA, citing a “thorough review of prior associations” without naming them. The linked account reports Laura Loomer’s speculation that Isaacman’s friendship with Elon Musk contributed to the decision. The White House said a replacement would be announced, but the review findings and Senate status remain unclear.
description_long:
On May 31, 2025, Trump withdrew Jared Isaacman’s nomination to lead NASA. The public explanation cited a “thorough review of prior associations” but did not identify the relationships or findings involved. Isaacman was a billionaire and chief executive of payment-processing company Shift4. Conservative commentator Laura Loomer suggested that his friendship with Elon Musk contributed to the withdrawal, but that was speculation rather than an explanation issued by Trump.

Reuters reported that the White House said a replacement nominee would be announced soon and described the decision as bad news for NASA, according to an astronomer it interviewed. The reports reviewed here do not identify what the administration’s review found or state what action the Senate had taken on Isaacman’s nomination when it was withdrawn. Those details are needed to distinguish the stated rationale from speculation about Musk and to establish the nomination’s procedural status. The documented action is the withdrawal; its specific basis and Senate timeline remain unclear.

preserved_fields.title: Trump pulls nomination of NASA head for no clear reason
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump pulls nomination of NASA head for no clear reason

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile article and Reuters coverage. They confirm the May 31 withdrawal, Trump’s phrase “thorough review of prior associations,” Loomer’s Musk-related speculation, and the White House’s plan to name a replacement. Neither reports the review’s findings or the Senate’s procedural status at withdrawal, so the reason and nomination timeline remain unresolved.

title: Trump: RFK Jr. fires all CDC vaccine panel members
description_short: Trump: RFK Jr. fires all CDC vaccine panel members
description_medium: On June 9, 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. dismissed all 17 members of the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, days before its scheduled June 25 meeting. HHS said the meeting would proceed. The decision reversed Kennedy’s confirmation-hearing assurance to Senator Bill Cassidy that he would not alter the panel; the committee’s recommendations affect vaccine access.
description_long:
On June 9, 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the panel that advises the agency on vaccine policy. HHS said the committee’s June 25 meeting would proceed, although replacements had not yet been announced.

The decision reversed Kennedy’s assurance to Senator Bill Cassidy during his confirmation hearings that he would not change the panel. Kennedy later argued that members had pharmaceutical conflicts of interest. The linked account said ACIP members were screened for conflicts and barred from holding vaccine-company stock or serving on manufacturers’ boards. The timing also left uncertainty about the committee’s review after the CDC changed its COVID-19 vaccine recommendation for pregnant women; the June meeting was expected to address the issue. Removing the members changed who would advise the agency on vaccine recommendations, but did not itself decide the scientific merits of a vaccine or establish that every former member was free of conflicts.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

preserved_fields.title: Trump: RFK Jr. fires all CDC vaccine panel members
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: RFK Jr. fires all CDC vaccine panel members
